rules.sentence: Lichen nitidus has definitive histopathological characteristics.

The hallmark of lichen nitidus is a well-circumscribed granulomatous infiltrate of lymphocytes, macrophages, Langerhans giant cells, and multinucleated epithelioid histiocytes in the papillary dermis bordered by extensions of epidermal ridges.
Early lichen nitidus lesions have more lymphocytes present, while later lesions are more granulomatous with occasional giant cells noted.
The epidermis is thinned and parakeratotic with hydropic degeneration of basal keratinocytes and cytoid bodies.
Generalized purpuric lichen nitidus has the same histopathological features as lichen nitidus in addition to subepidermal hemorrhages.
Lichen planus has more uniform lymphocytes within the infiltrate that makes up mostly T helper cells (CD4+).
Lichen nitidus usually presents as asymptomatic, shiny, flat-topped, fleshy pink to dark brown papules.
If lichen nitidus is symptomatic, the patient mainly complains of mild sporadic pruritus.
Koebner phenomenon is a hallmark of lichen nitidus, as seen in lichen planus, but is not present in all cases.
